Consider the rectangular region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le \sqrt{3},\,\,0\le v\le \frac{\pi }{2}},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v).
$$

Which of the following could be the image of the right side of $Δ$ under the action of $T?$

choices.value: The image is the empty set

Consider the rectangular region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,1\le u\le \sqrt{3},\,\,\frac{\pi }{6}\le v\le \frac{\pi }{2}},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v).
$$

Which of the following could be the image of the left side of $Δ$ under the action of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the left side.

For the left side, we have $u=1$ and $\frac{\pi }{6}\le v\le \frac{\pi }{2}.$ 

Substituting $u=1$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v) \\  & =(1\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,1\operatorname{sin}⁡v) \\  & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{\pi }{6}\le v\le \frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

This is an equation of a circular arc of radius $1$ centered at the origin in the $xy$-plane. 
The arc lies in the first quadrant between the polar rays $\theta =\frac{\pi }{6}$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{2},$ as shown below.
